data.review_text:
Buyer beware: Temu's "rewards" are a bait-and-switch
Temu lures you in with promises of cash, credits, or vouchers — but the payout is always just out of reach. Every time you get close to redeeming a reward, the app asks for another purchase, another referral, another step. It's an endless loop designed to keep you spending, not to actually reward you.
This isn't just my own experience — several state attorneys general (Arizona, Arkansas, Oklahoma, Nebraska, Texas) have filed lawsuits alleging Temu uses exactly this kind of bait-and-switch scheme to lure users in with prizes that never arrive. The FTC has also taken enforcement action over Temu's gamified shopping tactics. Save yourself the frustration — don't count on ever cashing out.

data.review_title: Temu Fraud & One month later, complaint not resolved.
data.review_text:
I filed a complaint and ticket with Temu over a month ago after fraud was committed by Temu themselves.  After more than a month, the issue is still not resolved.  What legitimate company does not deal with a complaint after a full month. Instead they just send and respond to emails saying someone will deal with it soon.  It is clear they have no intention of doing so.

Temu gets 0 Stars, but unfortunately that is not an option available. They committed fraud & bait & switch.

Two major issues. First, Temu processed an order I did NOT make. I had put some items in my cart, but I didn't process the order.  When later I saw an email saying payment had been taken and an order had been initiated, I contacted them to inform them I did NOT make the order and to cancel the order.  They refused, despite the fact that alleged 'order' had just been made and obviously it hadn't been processed and it certainly hadn't been shipped.  Surprise, Surprise.  Obviously they didn't want to refund the order, because the order had been fraudulently taken in the first place.  It was within the 14 days on an online 'purchase' (so I had a right to cancel), I didn't make the order in the first place (so they should have refunded a payment they were not allowed to take) and it hadn't been processed or shipped (so they should have refunded my money immediately). Instead they sent an order I didn't want.  

Second, they promised me SIX FREE GIFTS, but then didn't give the gifts and later said I didn't get the gifts because I need to spend a certain amount of money to get the gifts.  It didn't say that when the gifts were being offered and I spent about 1.5 hours choosing my gifts. This is called "Bait and Switch" which is highly illegal.  However, later the gifts were not offered to me or sent to me. I have been in several conversations with customer service since and they refuse to help me.  They just keep going round and round in circles.  

To start with, they sent the items I didn't order.  Then they refuse to refund the order and also refuse to send the 6 free gifts.  I made a formal complaint and they promised a manager would contact me in a few hours.  Instead it has been more than a month and they keep delaying further days. They have wasted so much of my time and caused so much stress. 

I reminded them of the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 (CPRs). ​This law contains a "Blacklist" of 31 commercial practices that are banned in all circumstances, regardless of what the fine print says.

​Banned Practice #20: It is completely illegal to describe a product as "gratis", "free", "without charge", or similar if the consumer has to pay anything other than the unavoidable cost of responding to the advertisement or collecting/paying for delivery of the item.

​Banned Practice #6 ("Bait-and-Switch"): It is illegal to promote a specific product at a specific price (or for free) if the business actually intends to substitute it with a different requirement or force you into a different commercial transaction (like buying other goods to "unlock" it).  

Despite this reminder they remained unphased.

I am warning you, never give Temu your payment details or name or contact details.  They are a dodgy company and do not have an issue with committing fraud.  Who knows what else they are doing with your details. Never fall for their free gifts trick.  It is a scam.

Steer far clear from Temu!!!

data.review_text:
RESPUESTA A TEMU:Hola Temu!!
Gracias por responder. Les proporciono más detalles sobre mi experiencia con Temu, concretamente sobre el sistema de vales de descuento, que considero engañoso y una práctica de venta desleal.
Cuando entro a la aplicación o página web, Temu muestra vales de descuento (por ejemplo, "10% de descuento", "cupón de X€") que parecen aplicables a cualquier compra. Sin embargo, en el momento de pagar, el sistema no permite usarlos directamente: obliga a seguir añadiendo productos al carrito, subiendo el importe mínimo requerido, o completando "misiones" (como jugar a ruletas, invitar a amigos, ver anuncios, etc.) para poder desbloquear el descuento prometido. Esto genera confusión deliberada durante el proceso de pago, ya que el cliente cree que va a pagar un precio y, al final, se encuentra con condiciones ocultas o cambiantes que le empujan a gastar más de lo que pretendía inicialmente.
En mi caso concreto, 25 de Julio del 2026, , intenté usar un vale de 9 euros y un descuento de 12’90 en mi pedido recogido en el carrito, por un total de 35 euros y con descuentos se quedaba en 5 euros o algo asi, lo cual me obligaba a comprar mas artículos hasta llegar a los 20 euros. Al llegar a la pantalla de pago, el descuento desapareció o se me indicó que debía añadir más artículos para poder aplicarlo, algo que no se explicaba con claridad en el momento en que se ofreció el vale.
Hice una captura de pantalla parcial que tomé en el momento, aunque no cuenta con la mejor calidad ni recoge el proceso completo, ya que en su momento no pensé en documentar cada paso. Aun así, se mira borrosa y por eso no la puedo enviar.
Considero que esta práctica:
1.	Induce a error al consumidor, mostrando descuentos que no son realmente aplicables sin condiciones adicionales no informadas de forma clara y previa.
2.	Presiona a comprar más de lo necesario, mediante técnicas de "dark pattern" (patrones oscuros de diseño) diseñadas para confundir en el momento crítico del pago.
3.	Puede vulnerar la normativa de protección al consumidor, en concreto la normativa sobre prácticas comerciales engañosas y transparencia en las condiciones de descuentos y ofertas.
Solicito que Temu explique con claridad, y de forma pública, en qué condiciones reales se pueden aplicar estos vales de descuento, y que corrija esta práctica que considero engañosa para los consumidores.

data.review_text:

With the recent nice weather, I was really looking forward to enjoying it in the garden with friends.
Instead, I received a completely different item – a cheap, standard sheet-metal barbecue grill.
As soon as the parcel arrived, we opened the box, immediately saw it was not the item that had been advertised, and closed it again to request a return and full refund. It has now been three weeks of writing to both Temu Support and the seller, Home Interiors Hinckley, almost every day, yet they have still failed to provide the return documents or resolve the issue.

Temu's customer support has been completely ineffective. We have chatted with 26 different support agents, but none has been able to resolve what should have been a straightforward case of receiving the wrong item.

I am extremely disappointed with both the seller for false advertising and Temu for its appalling lack of customer service. Save your money and shop elsewhere. In my experience, Temu is only worth considering for items under £3

I’m rating the Temu app with a NEGATIVE 5 based on its EXTREME persistence to push you to buy with the spinning wheels and flash fast messages no matter how many times you try closing the “game” windows. Every time you hit to close out ANOTHER game window pops up insisting that you “spin the wheel”. The other thing that is concerning is the excessive texts you receive from them, especially the ones stating that because you’re such a great customer and they’re “feeling generous” they are “reimbursing your purchase”. To be clear, the definition of reimbursement means ‘to return monies [you’ve spent] on a purchase’. I fell for that trap thinking I was actually receiving money back from Temu because the price on an item I bought had dropped between the time I purchased the item/s and the time it shipped. No! I had to then go through the process of requesting a refund for what they charged to my account!! This happened day before yesterday.
I did some research on Temu and their horrible performance and will take the suggestion of someone else who was taken in by their ploys and delete my account and block them from texting me. IF I feel to buy more of what I previously bought I’ll only shop through my private browser, using an entirely separate account and private phone number.
Next, my purchases: I have bought women’s pjs, pants, sneakers and rechargeable lights, a tiny air cooler fan system with a water misting capability, a cat toy and some other small things that I’m truly happy with. But I *have* found MANY sellers that have padded their items with fake or several times reposted “customer” reviews to try fooling you into thinking the item is a 5 star perfect purchase. Often you’ll see the EXACT product pictured several times but under a different seller name for either more or very slightly less than the price you looked at. BEWARE!! I’ve reported those and blocked them but I don’t have confidence that Temu’s “security” actually follows through on those alerts.
So far, I’ve received my items in good shape, secured boxing and in ziplock bags for the clothing. But they need to do MUCH better overall.

data.review_title: I used to be a regular customer
data.review_text: I used to be a regular customer, but after my recent experiences with Temu, I strongly advise everyone to be extremely cautious. Temu heavily advertises their "Local Warehouse" delivery as a major feature, but in reality, you pay the exact same price (or sometimes higher) as you would on major marketplaces like Amazon. The difference is that Amazon delivers the item the same day or next day, while Temu's "local" package takes weeks to arrive from halfway across the country, completely missing their guaranteed delivery windows. On top of that, most items are extremely low quality—what looks decent in pictures turns out to be cheap trash. The app is also filled with predatory and manipulative games like Farmland and Fishland designed to waste your time and trick you into buying useless items. When a package is delayed past the contract deadline or misdelivered, customer service becomes a complete nightmare. I spent 3.5 hours in support chats being repeatedly gaslighted. They accept invalid "proof of delivery" photos (like a package sitting on a driver's lap in their vehicle or generic photos without unit numbers) while demanding buyers file police reports for minor missing items. Even when you explicitly cancel an order due to a breach of delivery terms, they ignore you, force the late package onto your doorstep, and refuse a proper refund. To make matters worse, instead of returning funds to the original payment card they unlawfully dump it into Temu Credits to trap your money in their ecosystem. I have had to file formal claims with the Better Business Bureau (BBB) and initiate bank disputes to get my money back. Temu lies even in their official responses to regulators, claiming "no record of cancellation" despite hours of documented chat history. Avoid this platform—the savings are fake, the logistics are unreliable, and the customer service is predatory.
